question: Why is the Kula-born woman not recognized as embodying Kula across all classes?
premises: The Kula-born woman is the subject
She is not known or recognized
Her nature spans the multitude of classes and Kula
inference: The Kula-born woman, whose nature encompasses all classes and Kula, remains unrecognized.
uncertainties: the rhetorical force of kiṃ na may imply affirmation or lament
plain_english: How is the Kula-born woman not known, she whose nature is Kula across the multitude of all classes?
